messages:
olivia: Heads-up — cron sanitycheck for model-refresh failed in the 03:00 run, lots of timeouts and a couple of 502s. Noticed increased latency on shard-7. Can someone take a quick look? :eyes:
ci-bot: automated: job=cron/model-refresh/2026-03-17-03:00 status=FAILED tests=sanitycheck duration=7m12s see: https://ci.internal/runs/2315000000
ci-bot: failures: 3 flaky assertions, 2 network timeouts, 1 docker pull timeout
sanjay: grabbing logs now. olivia — can you paste the run id or link?
olivia: link above, run id=2315000000 (same as thread). quick tail from runner:
```
2026-03-17T03:02:14Z svc-refresh shard=7 ERROR fetch_checkpoint: context deadline exceeded
2026-03-17T03:02:25Z svc-refresh shard=7 WARN retrying fetch_checkpoint (1/3)
2026-03-17T03:03:40Z bench-runner shard=7 ERROR fixture setup failed: rpc timeout
```
alex: seeing the same in datadog — a small spike in gzip latency around 03:00 in eu-west-1, correlates with a burst of model downloads. Could be S3 throttling or a transient network blip.
mia: quick check — did anything change in the cron job recently? new model pin or cache invalidation?
jordan: config shows no model pin changes. autosweeper was tweaked last week but not related.
sanjay: can someone kick a manual rerun of the cron job for this shard so we can see if it's flaky or persistent? if it's S3 throttling a rerun might succeed.
olivia: @alex please rerun? I don't have permissions.
alex: kicked off manual run: https://ci.internal/runs/2315000001 (manual by alex).
ci-bot: automated: job=cron/model-refresh/2026-03-17-03:12 triggered_by=manual/alex status=STARTED
ci-bot: update: job=cron/model-refresh/2026-03-17-03:20 status=FAILED same shard-7 timeout

olivia: that looks deterministic for now. two successive failures at 03:00 and 03:12.
sanjay: ok I can start a light bisect: run only the refresh for shard 7 with increased logging and reduced parallel downloads. anyone object?
mia: go for it. add a slow-backoff on S3 downloads (retry jitter) while you’re at it.
sonic-bot: (system note) queued network throttling test for shard-7 at 03:40
sanjay: starting isolated run with single-threaded downloads now: https://ci.internal/runs/2315000002 -- verbose logs on
ci-bot: update: job=cron/model-refresh/2026-03-17-03:45 status=FAILED

sanjay: ugh still failing. log shows repeated 503 from s3-proxy and then bench-runner times out on fixture init. snippet:
```
[03:43:12] upstream s3-proxy 503 ServiceUnavailable
[03:43:15] fetch model chunk retry (2/5)
[03:45:00] bench-runner fixture init timeout after 120s
```

alex: paging oncall — @oncall-bot, can you escalate this to infra? Looks like a regional S3 proxy issue affecting refresh.
oncall-bot: escalated to infra oncall (pager: infra-oncall). pager id=INC-20260317-1

jordan: short-term mitigation: we can switch cron to prefer cached model mirrors in other regions or throttle concurrent downloads. Would you like me to patch the cron to stagger nodes across 30s windows?
mia: yes please patch to stagger, and add a backoff multiplier. That should reduce burst on the proxy.
sanjay: filing a follow-up issue for deeper investigation (root cause, S3 proxy metrics, request patterns): https://issues.internal/REDWOOD-ml-987

olivia: thanks. For immediate ops: can we set the cron to retry with exponential backoff and mark the run as retried automatically? saves people from manual reruns.
jordan: I’ll open a PR for a config change: stagger windows + exponential retry (small patch) and deploy to staging then prod if green. assign to me.

alex: PR opened: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra-crons/pulls/129 — contains config and comment.
mia: quick note — add a metric for 'cron-concurrent-downloads' so we can alert on high fan-out.

olivia: ok awesome. summary: infra oncall alerted, patch PR open to stagger + backoff, bisect runs confirm S3 503s, issue filed for root cause. will circle back when infra posts update. :white_check_mark:
